articles.title: investingLive Americas FX news wrap 9 Oct: It’s a Wrap: Stocks rebound despite weak sentiment; Canadian dollar falls on jobs miss
articles.desc: US stocks close higher; Nasdaq gains for fourth straight week Week ahead: US inflation and retail sales lead a busy economic calendar. Be aware. Let's Play... "More Bullish or More Bearish". How would I view the technicals for the Mag 7 stocks. This week we got a sneak-peak at the playbook for when
articles.content: US stocks close higher; Nasdaq gains for fourth straight week Week ahead: US inflation and retail sales lead a busy economic calendar. Be aware. Let's Play... "More Bullish or More Bearish". How would I view the technicals for the Mag 7 stocks. This week we got a sneak-peak at the playbook for when the AI bubble bursts What's open and closed in US and Canadian markets on Monday Bakers Hughes total rig count +5 to 603 European stocks finish higher Friday, but most post weekly declines SpaceX lockup expiration puts buyers to the test. The technicals define the risk. JPMorgan: The G7’s 100 million barrel oil release is mostly old barrels with a new bow on it Broader stock indices bouncing modestly. Support near 100 hour MAs held yesterday US October UMich prelim consumer sentiment 46.3 vs 47.8 expected Bitcoin sellers had their shot. They missed. Canada September employment change -68.3K vs +9.2K expected Morning Kickstart: Dollar mixed, stocks rebound and oil retreats amid Iran uncertainty Bessent hires former Fed board nominee and investingLive reader, Judy Shelton as adviser investingLive European session wrap: Stocks rebound as bond market nerves ease, for now How have interest rate expectations changed after this week's events? U.S. stock buyers had a better day on Friday. After Thursday’s selling tied to concerns over AI revenues, all five major indices finished higher, with the Dow leading the percentage gains. The economic news was less encouraging. U.S. consumer sentiment disappointed while inflation expectations edged higher. Canada lost another 68,300 jobs, pushing the Canadian dollar lower. Nevertheless, stocks, precious metals and Bitcoin all advanced into the weekend. Dollar mixed; Canadian dollar hurt by employment report The dollar finished mixed. It was strongest against the Canadian dollar and Japanese yen, gaining about 0.25% against each, and weakest against the Australian dollar. The late-session snapshot of the major currency pairs showed: EURUSD: 1.1201, −0.07%. USDJPY: 158.26, +0.25%. GBPUSD: 1.3233, +0.07%. USDCHF: 0.8300, −0.17%. USDCAD: 1.4261, +0.25%. AUDUSD: 0.6985, +0.43%. NZDUSD: 0.5613, +0.05%. USDCAD jumped from around 1.4232 before the Canadian employment report to near 1.4293 afterward. Some of that gain was retraced, but the Canadian dollar remained under pressure. Treasury curve flattens Treasury yields were mixed near the close, with shorter maturities moving higher while the 30-year yield edged lower: 2-year: 4.7911%, +3.51 basis points. 5-year: 5.0211%, +3.01 basis points. 10-year: 5.2441%, +1.11 basis points. 30-year: 5.6001%, −0.69 basis point. That combination flattened the curve. The rise in near-term inflation expectations gave traders another reason to remain cautious about the inflation outlook, even with consumer sentiment weakening. U.S. stocks finish higher The major indices closed higher across the board: Dow industrial average: 51,660.18, +423.06 points or +0.83%. S&P 500: 7,811.54, +46.18 points or +0.59%. Nasdaq Composite: 27,366.17, +172.83 points or +0.64%. Russell 2000: 2,806.9815, +12.8535 points or +0.46%. Nasdaq 100: 30,883.15, +157.34 points or +0.51%. The rebound extended beyond technology, with the Dow outperforming and small caps also participating. Still, one positive session does not remove the questions surrounding AI spending, revenues and valuations. In Adam’s afternoon review, he highlighted that Thursday’s OpenAI revenue comparison required an adjustment for partner revenue. He also noted that the dollar fell alongside AI shares during the initial reaction—an unusual response for a currency that often benefits when risk assets decline. That relationship bears watching. It's European stocks also finished Friday higher: Germany’s DAX: 25,087.28, +1.13%. France’s CAC: 7,803.34, +0.95%. UK’s FTSE 100: 10,552.04, +1.06%. Spain’s IBEX: 19,033.10, +0.55%. Italy’s FTSE MIB: 49,746.30, +0.91%. Friday’s gains were not enough to erase weekly losses in most markets. Italy fell 1.46%, France declined 1.19%, Germany lost 0.57% and Spain slipped 0.27%. The UK bucked the trend with a 0.86% gain. French unrest and fiscal uncertainty remained part of the European backdrop. See the European close review here. Michigan sentiment falls; inflation expectations rise The preliminary October University of Michigan consumer sentiment index fell to 46.3 from 48.1, below the 47.8 estimate. Current conditions were particularly weak at 44.7 versus 51.0 expected. Expectations were better than forecast at 47.3 versus 45.5. For the Fed, the inflation expectations figures remain the concern: One-year expectations: 4.7%, up from 4.6%. Five-year expectations: 3.5%, up from 3.4%. Consumers are feeling worse, but they are also expecting higher prices. That is an uncomfortable combination for policymakers, but is the fear greater than the reality? The headline was deeply depressed, although it remained above the 44.8 May low cited in the report. Next week, we get CPI and PPI data which combined will help to calculate the PCE. Canada loses another 68.3K jobs Canada’s September employment report missed expectations for a 9.2K increase with a sharp decline of 68.3K. Following August’s 41.7K decline, the two-month loss reached 110K. Full-time employment fell 35,400 and part-time employment declined 32,900. The unemployment rate rose to 6.5% from 6.4%, while participation slipped to 64.8% from 65.0%. The participation decline limited the increase in unemployment. There were some qualifications to the weak headline. Public-sector employment fell 70,000, while private-sector employment rose 24,100. Education and youth employment declines also raised questions about seasonal adjustments around the return to school. Nevertheless, another large employment decline is difficult to ignore. Permanent employees’ wage growth also increased to 2.3% from 2.0%, adding a complication for the Bank of Canada. Oil little changed; Iran remains a weekend risk WTI crude futures were near $91.50 in the supplied snapshot, up $0.01 or 0.01%. Earlier relief followed President Trump’s comments that discussions with Iran were productive and that attacks on Tehran would be deferred until after the midterm elections. That helped reduce the immediate escalation premium, but it did not resolve the conflict or the risks to energy supplies. The afternoon Baker Hughes report showed total U.S. rigs rising by 5 to 603, including a 6-rig increase in oil rigs to 462. Gold and silver advance Precious metals posted solid gains in the late-session snapshot: Spot gold: $4,196.065, +$62.375 or +1.51%. Silver: $60.7912, +$1.6107 or +2.72%. Gold advanced despite higher 2-, 5- and 10-year yields. The mixed dollar and slightly lower 30-year yield offered a less uniform headwind, but the strength in metals also suggests demand extended beyond a simple interest-rate trade. Rising inflation expectations may have contributed, although the snapshot alone cannot establish the driver. Bitcoin edges higher Bitcoin traded near $82,316, up $640 or 0.78%. The gain was consistent with the recovery in equities. It was a better day for risk assets, although Bitcoin’s move did not establish a separate trend from broader markets. See the latest technically HERE. What carries into next week? Stocks recovered, but inflation concerns and questions over AI economics remain. Canadian employment weakness adds another issue for currency traders, while Middle East headlines retain the potential to change the mood over the weekend. Monday brings a split holiday session: U.S. stocks will trade normally, the U.S. bond market will be closed, and Canadian markets will close for Thanksgiving. That leaves traders facing potentially thinner conditions as the new week begins. See what’s open and closed here. This article was written by Greg Michalowski at investinglive.com.

articles.title: WATCH - 'It’s been a long time coming' - popular chicken giant opens in York
articles.desc: A popular fast-food chain has opened its doors on a brand new York location.
articles.content: Popeyes fried chicken opens in Church Street, York | York Press Popeyes fried chicken opens in Church Street, York This article is brought to you by our exclusive subscriber partnership with our sister title USA Today, and has been written by our American colleagues. It does not necessarily reflect the view of The Herald. A POPULAR fast-food chain has opened its doors in York. Popeyes – a popular New Orleans style fried chicken chain – has officially opened to the public with around 100 people waiting in line to get the first taste of the American fast-food staple known for catering Beyonce’s wedding. The opening, which took place at 11am today (October 9) saw a full brass brand performing, merchandise giveaways, and free chicken burgers being handed out to the first 100 inside the new restaurant. PICTURES - Salon which transports visitors to 'another world' opens in York Band behind iconic Grammy winning album to open tour in York The new restaurant, located inside the former Game shop, has created 70 jobs in the city and offers dine in options, including delivery to the table, along with takeaway and delivery. Popeyes have also launched a new rewards app with 2000 extra points for each person who signs up in the York restaurant over the weekend. First in the queue was Teigan Butterfield from , who along with her partner Jude and friend Simon, had been waiting outside since 6pm the day before (October 8), with the promise of free chicken sandwiches for a year in return for their efforts. She said that the idea to line up came from a friend who told her about his experience being first in line at two other Popeyes openings - making her want to try it for herself. She said: “It’s been a crazy night sitting out here. The weather wasn’t too bad as we’re under the canopy, but there’s been a lot of shenanigans going on around here all night. “We had someone come up to us and talk at us for 90 minutes, and the local homeless people in the area have come to check that we were okay – which was really nice. “Originally, there was four of us here, but one guy ended up leaving because he said it was too tough, and then we’ve had a few more people join us at midnight. Normally, they only give it to the first three people, but they’ve been really nice and made sure all six of us got it. “I didn’t get any sleep. I’m actually meant to be at uni in a few hours, but I don’t think that’s going to happen after tonight.” After tasting her burger, she confirmed that the burger was “banging” and “miles ahead of the other competitors, who we will not name.” Tom Crowley, CEO of Popeyes UK, said: “We’ve been trying to get to York a long time, it's a great city, but it's one of those locations where it's hard to find the right property. “We were so pleased to finally find the right spot, right on the corner here which is amazing, and we’ve had such a good response here. I’ve done this since day one up and down the country and it’s a bit of a phenomenon. “The brand has such heritage – it’s 50 years, right out of New Orleans, and it’s one of the biggest brands in the US. It’s nice when people come and try our products and have that big ‘wow, okay’ reaction. We want to just bring a little slice of New Orleans to the city.” This was echoed by James Clark, Head of Digital Marketing for Popeyes, who is originally from York and was ‘delighted’ to see the opening in his hometown. He added: “It’s been a long time coming. York is definitely one of the biggest cities that we haven’t opened in and the reaction has been amazing – it’s a great thing for the city and it’s a really great location.” Popeyes is open from 10.30am to 11pm daily. articles.title: Valion Bio (Nasdaq:VBIO): Oral Mucosal Entolimod Could Offer a New Needle-Free Deployment Path to Support Growing Need for Scalable Civilian Radiation Preparedness Should Nuclear Infrastructure Expand to Support Data Centers
articles.content: Valion Bio (Nasdaq:VBIO): Oral Mucosal Entolimod Could Offer a New Needle-Free Deployment Path to Support Growing Need for Scalable Civilian Radiation Preparedness Should Nuclear Infrastructure Expand to Support Data Centers - BioSpace Valion Bio (Nasdaq:VBIO): Oral Mucosal Entolimod Could Offer a New Needle-Free Deployment Path to Support Growing Need for Scalable Civilian Radiation Preparedness Should Nuclear Infrastructure Expand to Support Data Centers Rising electricity demand from AI and data centers is driving plans to expand nuclear power capacity, possibly including on-site small modular reactors (SMRs)¹ Medical countermeasures need to scale along with that infrastructure Valion is developing an oral mucosal formulation of Entolimod that could potentially provide a needle-free administration option for acute radiation syndrome ("ARS") As nuclear power assumes an increasingly important role in meeting the growing electricity requirements of artificial intelligence, data centers and other digital infrastructure, the expansion of the U.S. nuclear-energy landscape that has been increasingly making across the country is also highlighting the importance of resilient emergency preparedness and medical countermeasures for potential radiological and nuclear events. Against this backdrop, Valion Bio, Inc. (Nasdaq:VBIO) ("Valion" or the "Company"), a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing biologics that activate innate immune pathways for cytoprotection, believes the evolving U.S. nuclear energy landscape reinforces the importance of advancing medical countermeasures that could be deployed rapidly and at population scale in the event of a radiological or nuclear emergency. "The significance of the changing nuclear landscape extends beyond how electricity is generated - it also raises important questions about how communities and emergency systems prepare for low-probability, high-consequence radiation events," said Dean Zikria, Interim Chief Executive Officer of Valion Bio. Entolimod, Valion's investigational drug biologic being developed for ARS is designed to potentially protect cells from severe damage or death both prophylactically (pre-exposure) and therapeutically (post-exposure). Historically administered by intramuscular injection, Entolimod is now the subject of an oral mucosal formulation-development program with Shear Kershman Laboratories ("SKL") utilizing SKL's proprietary BioViscid™ drug-delivery platform. successfully completed formulation work under their ongoing program to develop a novel oral mucosal formulation of Entolimod. The resulting BioViscid™-Entolimod formulation is designed to enable absorption through the oral mucosa, potentially providing a needle-free alternative to injectable administration. If successfully developed and approved, Valion believes a needle-free formulation of Entolimod could potentially change how a radiation countermeasure is stored, distributed and administered. Potential operational advantages include: Utility potential before and after radiation exposure: Published animal studies of injected Entolimod have demonstrated protection against lethal radiation when administered before exposure, including protection involving both hematopoietic and gastrointestinal tissues. Separate non-human-primate research has reported improved survival and recovery of bone marrow and intestinal tissue when Entolimod was administered after radiation exposure. These findings support the scientific rationale for investigating Entolimod as a potential countermeasure across different phases of a radiation event. Current FDA-approved medical countermeasures for ARS address the hematopoietic, or bone-marrow, component of radiation injury in patients exposed to myelosuppressive doses of radiation. articles.content: Apple plans first touchscreen MacBook launch for October 27 Apple is planning to unveil its first touchscreen MacBook on October 27 The late-October event is also expected to include a new iPad mini with an OLED screen and updated iMac and MacBook Pro models with M6 chips is planning to introduce its first touchscreen MacBook at an event scheduled on or around October 27, according to . Journalists will be invited to attend in person, and the event will also be streamed online. According to Bloomberg, the redesigned MacBook Pro models — internally referred to as K114 and K116 — will shed weight compared to today's lineup and introduce OLED panels alongside the Dynamic Island, a feature previously exclusive to iPhones. The iPad mini, carrying the internal designation J510, is also on the agenda; it will gain an OLED display, move its front-facing camera to the long edge of the device, and receive a redesigned speaker setup. Also expected at the event are refreshed versions of the entry-level 14-inch MacBook Pro and iMac running 's new M6 chip. Those machines, code-named J804 and J833, will otherwise resemble their current designs, according to Bloomberg. The launch is aimed at creative professionals in video production, photo editing, and music production, according to Bloomberg. held a similar in-person press showcase for new Macs in Los Angeles in 2024. The company is also scheduled to hold a smart home-focused event on October 13, which is expected to include a home hub with a display, a new HomePod mini, and an updated Chief Executive John Ternus, who took over from Tim Cook last month, has been overseeing a wide slate of new hardware. unveiled its first foldable phone, the iPhone Duo, alongside the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max at the company's annual fall event in September, where Ternus made his public debut leading the company. articles.title: Drivers urged to use this 'batch' trick to cut fuel costs
articles.desc: Car dealership Dace Motor Group has warned vehicle owners that making multiple short trips in a day could be causing Brits to burn through their fuel faster.
articles.content: Drivers urged to use this 'batch' trick to cut fuel costs | Wales Online Drivers urged to use this 'batch' trick to cut fuel costs Car dealership Dace Motor Group has warned vehicle owners that making multiple short trips in a day could be causing Brits to burn through their fuel faster. Drivers are being urged to 'batch' their daily errands to help save them money and reduce fuel consumption. Car dealership Dace Motor Group has warned vehicle owners that making multiple short trips in a day could be causing Brits to burn through their fuel faster. This is because nipping out in your car on several separate occasions instead of just one means you're starting your engine up from cold every time. When an engine is cold it is least sufficient as it is said to use more fuel than a warmed-up one. To combat this, Dace Motor Group is encouraging drivers to 'batch' all their daily errands into one large journey where possible. This is seen as more fuel-efficient as your engine will be warm and not have to heat up from scratch every time. The car retailer also suggests avoiding at peak times as this will help you dodge the worst traffic. By doing so you will also save on fuel as you'll spend less time burning through your petrol sitting in congestion. So next time you need to do a grocery shop, post a parcel and pick up your kids from , try and do it one large journey to save you some cash. On their website, Dace Motor Group said: "This one does sound too simple, but it works. A car is less efficient when the engine is cold. "So, if you do a quick dash to the shop, come home, then head back out for the chemist, then later pop to pick someone up, you are making the car do its least efficient bit again and again. The better move is to tie those jobs together in one run if you can. Pick grab the parcel, up the bread, swing by the supermarket, then head home. "Not every day lets you do that, of course. Life gets in the way. But even doing it a couple of times a week will help." The RAC also backs this driving hack as a way for Brits to cut down on fuel consumption. The RAC said: "Consider making one round trip rather than several short trips. "Once the engine is warm it will operate at its most efficient whereas several cold starts will increase fuel consumption even though the total mileage could be the same." articles.title: Apple vs Amazon vs Google: Who Will Win the Smart Home Race?
articles.desc: Apple vs Amazon vs Google: Compare smart home devices, AI assistants, home security, and automation to see who could lead the connected home market.
articles.content: Apple vs Amazon vs Google: Who Will Win the Smart Home Race? Apple vs Amazon vs Google: Who Will Win the Smart Home Race? Apple is Building A Smarter Home Ecosystem: Apple is working to make its smart home products fit closely with its iPhone, Apple Watch, and other devices. HomeKit and the Apple Home app let users control compatible lights, locks, cameras, and more. Its focus on privacy and smooth connections could help Apple attract people already using its products. Amazon Alexa Has A Strong Smart Home Presence: Amazon has built a broad smart home offering around Alexa, Echo speakers, and compatible devices from many brands. Users can control lights, manage routines, check cameras, and operate connected appliances through voice commands. This wide range of options gives Amazon an advantage among people who want flexibility and easy home automation. Google Home Brings Gemini Into The Picture: Google is expanding its smart home experience with Google Home, Nest devices, and Gemini-powered features. Its strength lies in combining voice controls, search technology, and AI to make everyday tasks easier. If Google can improve natural conversations and device control, it could make connected homes feel more useful and less complicated. Apple Could Win Through Privacy And Integration: Apple's biggest advantage may be how its products work together. Users can manage compatible smart home devices through Apple Home and control them using Siri. Apple also promotes privacy-focused features and secure connections. However, its success will depend on expanding device support, improving voice assistance, and making its ecosystem appealing to more households. Amazon Could Lead With Device Choice And Alexa: Amazon's wide range of Echo products and third-party smart home devices gives customers plenty of choices at different prices. Alexa also supports routines that connect multiple devices and automate daily tasks. Amazon could strengthen its position further by making Alexa more capable with AI while keeping setup simple for new smart home users. Google Could Stand Out With Smarter AI: Google has an opportunity to stand out by making Gemini more helpful in everyday home settings. A capable assistant could understand complex requests, manage several devices, and respond more naturally. Google's experience with AI and connected services gives it a strong starting point, but reliable controls and broad device compatibility remain essential. Who Will Win The Smart Home Race?: There may not be one clear winner because each company serves different needs. Apple appeals to users who value privacy and ecosystem integration, Amazon offers broad device choice, and Google brings AI expertise. articles.title: Seaport Therapeutics Presents Additional Pharmacokinetic Data from Phase 1 Clinical Trial of GlyphAgo™ at the 39th European College of Neuropsychopharmacology (ECNP) Congress
articles.content: Seaport Therapeutics Presents Additional Pharmacokinetic Data from Phase 1 Clinical Trial of GlyphAgo™ at the 39th European College of Neuropsychopharmacology (ECNP) Congress - BioSpace Seaport Therapeutics Presents Additional Pharmacokinetic Data from Phase 1 Clinical Trial of GlyphAgo™ at the 39th European College of Neuropsychopharmacology (ECNP) Congress First scientific presentation of detailed PK data demonstrates dose-dependent increases in agomelatine exposure, no food effect, and no accumulation of exposure over seven days of dosing Detailed data reinforces previously reported topline results demonstrating that GlyphAgo achieved a statistically significant 6.8-fold increase in agomelatine bioavailability and substantially lower (10-fold) PK variability compared to unmodified agomelatine Agomelatine levels comparable to those seen with efficacious doses of the unmodified drug were achieved at substantially lower doses, intended to reduce hepatic exposure and the potential for liver enzyme elevations (Nasdaq: SPTX) (“Seaport” or the “Company”), a clinical-stage therapeutics company developing novel neuropsychiatric medicines, today announced the presentation of Phase 1 clinical data for GlyphAgo™ (SPT-320 or Glyph Agomelatine) at the 39th European College of Neuropsychopharmacology (ECNP) Congress, taking place October 10-13, 2026, in Munich, Germany. The poster represents the first scientific presentation of data from the GlyphAgo Phase 1 program and provides detailed pharmacokinetic (PK) analyses supporting previously reported topline results and reinforcing GlyphAgo's differentiated profile. GlyphAgo is a novel, “Glyphed” oral prodrug of agomelatine designed to enhance lymphatic absorption and bypass first-pass liver metabolism. In the Phase 1 program, GlyphAgo demonstrated a statistically significant 6.8-fold increase in bioavailability of agomelatine compared to unmodified agomelatine and showed significantly lower (10-fold) PK variability. GlyphAgo achieved therapeutically relevant exposure of agomelatine at substantially lower doses that are designed to reduce liver exposure. Seaport believes this approach has the potential to reduce the risk of liver enzyme elevations and reduce the need for routine liver function monitoring that has historically limited agomelatine’s clinical use. “The data presented at ECNP provide important clinical validation that our Glyph™ platform can meaningfully improve the pharmacokinetic profile of medicines historically limited by high first-pass liver metabolism,” said Daniel Bonner, Ph.D., Co-Founder and Senior Vice President, Platform, at Seaport Therapeutics. “The increased exposure and markedly reduced inter-individual variability observed in the Phase 1 program are particularly compelling. More predictable drug exposure may translate into more consistent clinical outcomes for patients, further supporting the development of GlyphAgo as a potential treatment for generalized anxiety disorder.” The completed multi-part Phase 1 proof-of-concept trial evaluated the safety, tolerability and pharmacokinetics of GlyphAgo in 174 healthy volunteers. The newly presented results include data from the multiple-ascending dose (MAD) portion and analyses supporting the absence of a food effect with GlyphAgo. The single- and multiple-ascending dose portions of the trial demonstrated dose-dependent increases in agomelatine exposure and showed no accumulation of exposure over seven days of dosing, supporting a consistent profile with repeat dosing. Additional analyses presented in the poster further characterize the substantially reduced PK variability observed with GlyphAgo, with variability in both AUC₀-₂₄ and Cmax substantially lower than with unmodified agomelatine. Specifically, in the SAD portion, PK variability (geometric CV%) observed in participants dosed with GlyphAgo ranged from 12.9% to 26.6% for AUC₀-₂₄ and from 17.1% to 50.5% for Cmax, compared with 200% and 217%, respectively, for u

articles.title: Iran’s presence in world’s top 2% of scientists nearly doubles
articles.desc: TEHRAN – The number of Iranian researchers included in the world’s top 2% of scientists has nearly doubled, rising from 1,154 in 2020 to 2,678 in 2026, according to Scopus data provided by Elsevier.
articles.content: Iran’s presence in world’s top 2% of scientists nearly doubles - Tehran Times Iran’s presence in world’s top 2% of scientists nearly doubles TEHRAN – The number of Iranian researchers included in the world’s top 2% of scientists has nearly doubled, rising from 1,154 in 2020 to 2,678 in 2026, according to Scopus data provided by Elsevier. An analysis of the rankings shows a steady upward trend in the number of Iranian researchers recognized among the world’s top 2% of scientists over the past several years. The number rose to 1,701 in 2021 and 1,941 in 2022, before increasing to 2,137 in 2023 and 2,514 in 2024. The figure reached 2,678 in 2026, ISNA reported. The majority of Iranian researchers are from 30 universities and scientific centers; the University of Tehran, with 123 researchers, is placed first. Followed by Tehran University of Medical Sciences (112), Shahid Beheshti University of Medical Sciences (75), and Iran University of Science and Technology (74). Tabriz University of Medical Sciences with 66 researchers, Iran University of Medical Sciences with 64 researchers, University of Tabriz with 61 researchers, and Tarbiat Modares University with 56 researchers are placed fifth to eighth. Also, the number of highly cited Iranian researchers in the career-long index has experienced threefold growth, rising from 433 in 2020 to 1,380 in 2026. Some 794 out of 1,380 researchers, amounting to 57.5 percent, are from 30 universities and scientific centers. University of Tehran (with 91 researchers), Sharif University of Technology (53), Amirkabir University of Technology and Tehran University of Medical Sciences (each with 48 researchers), and Iran University of Science and Technology (45), University of Tabriz and Tarbiat Modares University (each with 40 researchers) rank first to fifth. Stanford University’s list of “World’s Top 2%” scientists is based on a 2 percent or above percentile rank, or the top 100,000 by c-score (with and without self-citations). This prestigious list identifies the world’s leading researchers, representing approximately 2 percent of all scientists worldwide. It encompasses standardised data on citations, h-index, and a wide range of bibliometric indicators. Researchers are classified into 22 scientific fields and 174 sub-fields, drawing from Scopus data provided by Elsevier through ICSR Lab. The esteemed ranking, derived from Scopus database data, highlights researchers whose work has had a significant impact across various scientific disciplines. The ranking is based on a composite indicator (c-score) calculated from six citation metrics: Total citations (NC), H-index (H), Hm-index (H-index adjusted for the number of authors), Citations to single-author papers (NCS), Citations to single or first-author papers (NCSF), Citations to single, first, or last-author papers (NCSFL). The c-score combines these metrics to provide a comprehensive measure of a scientist’s impact, accounting for both the quantity and the quality of their contributions. The list provides two separate rankings, each offering a different perspective on a researcher’s impact: Career-long impact ranking: This evaluates a researcher’s cumulative citation performance over their entire career to date. Single-year impact ranking: This focuses on the citation impact of research produced in the most recent year. Iran ranks first in key scientific output among Islamic countries Iran ranks first among Islamic nations in key fields of scientific output such as quantum science, cognitive sciences, artificial intelligence, biotechnology, and advanced materials, the head of the Presidential Affairs Office at the Islamic World Science Citation Center (ISC) announced in August. The country is in close competition with Turkey and Saudi Arabia in these fields, IRNA quoted Saeed Bakhtiari as saying. articles.title: New Phase 3b data on Lilly's Taltz (ixekizumab) and Zepbound (tirzepatide) advance understanding of the interconnected immune and metabolic biology in adults with psoriasis and obesity
articles.content: New Phase 3b data on Lilly's Taltz (ixekizumab) and Zepbound (tirzepatide) advance understanding of the interconnected immune and metabolic biology in adults with psoriasis and obesity - BioSpace New Phase 3b data on Lilly’s Taltz (ixekizumab) and Zepbound (tirzepatide) advance understanding of the interconnected immune and metabolic biology in adults with psoriasis and obesity Exploratory data presented at Fall Clinical 2026 showed broader biomarker changes with Taltz and Zepbound vs. Taltz alone as early as Week 12 in first-of-its-kind TOGETHER-PsO study /PRNewswire/ -- Eli Lilly and Company (NYSE: LLY) today announced new exploratory data from the TOGETHER-PsO Phase 3b clinical trial evaluating the concomitant use of Taltz (ixekizumab) and Zepbound (tirzepatide) compared with Taltz alone in adults with moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis and obesity or overweight with at least one additional weight-related comorbid condition. The prespecified analysis, presented at the 2026 Fall Clinical Dermatology Conference in Las Vegas, provides new insights suggesting an immunometabolic relationship between psoriasis and obesity. These data showed that when Taltz and Zepbound were used together, changes were observed in more psoriasis disease-associated and metabolic biomarkers compared to Taltz monotherapy. In the U.S., approximately 61% of people with psoriasis also have obesity or overweight with at least one weight-related comorbidity. "People living with psoriasis and obesity carry a compounded burden that extends beyond what is visible, yet these conditions are too often viewed through separate treatment lenses," said Mark Genovese, M.D., senior vice president of Lilly Immunology development. "The broader biomarker changes observed with Taltz and Zepbound, including those associated with skin clearance, may point to a meaningful relationship between immune and metabolic biology. Along with previously reported clinical outcomes, these findings support a more comprehensive approach to psoriasis care that also addresses obesity for people managing both conditions." This analysis examined circulating proteins and gene expression in the blood to better understand the biological change observed when patients were treated concomitantly with Taltz and Zepbound vs. Taltz alone. At Week 36, observed changes in psoriasis-specific, immune and metabolic biomarkers in both the Taltz and Zepbound and Taltz monotherapy treatment arms were consistent with the known biological effects of each medicine when used for their approved indications. Notably, Taltz and Zepbound used together were associated with broader biomarker responses compared to Taltz alone as early as Week 12. This included changes in more proteins (482 vs. 140 differentially expressed proteins) and genes (467 vs. 16 differentially expressed genes) by Week 36. Further, the analysis showed greater reductions in inflammatory immune activity with Taltz and Zepbound compared with Taltz alone, including changes related to neutrophils, a type of immune cell involved in inflammation. Changes in a subset of neutrophil-associated markers mediated a portion of the additional Psoriasis Area and Severity Index (PASI) response seen with Taltz and Zepbound vs. Taltz alone. "This analysis provides new insights into the potential connected immune and metabolic biology in people with psoriasis and obesity," said James G. Krueger, M.D., Ph.D., Professor and Laboratory Head, The Rockefeller University. "What is most compelling is these findings identified differences in inflammatory pathways when patients received concomitant treatment with Taltz plus Zepbound for both conditions. These data at the intersection of psoriasis and obesity highlight immunometabolic health as an important area for continued scientific research." from TOGETHER-PsO, which showed that Taltz and Zepbound used together delivered superior skin clearance and clinically meaningful weight reduction compared with Taltz alone at the
